topic_candidates.topic: CrazyBus video essay in my voice (clone VO + image assembly): 'The Bus That Was Never Supposed to Leave the Garage'
topic_candidates.reasoning: The full origin story (bus-horn forum post -> tech demo -> ROM sets -> YouTube fame -> DMCA trolls -> AVGN -> vanished creator) has never been told end-to-end in video; only the Bad Game Hall of Fame wrote it. Killer personal hook: the AVGN episode that made it famous was made by the man Garret met at Classic Game Fest. Proven pipeline twice (American Idol GBA, 131s essay). Moderate cost: image gens + clone VO + assembly.

topic_candidates.topic: Faithful CrazyBus homage playable: a bus that only goes left/right, honks, and plays pseudo-random PSG-style music (same tune every boot unless you mash buttons)
topic_candidates.reasoning: Playables are my proven cheap lane (Blackjack, Ember Beat, Dice & Depth, 3 shipped + playtested). Rebuilding 'the worst game ever' faithfully — including the deterministic-RNG music quirk — is a joke that lands twice: once for the game, once for the obsessive fidelity. Near-zero media cost (HTML/CSS/JS + WebAudio), fast to ship, and Garret gets to play it. The no-bluff spirit fits: it's a tech demo about a bus and it admits it.

topic_candidates.topic: Fable: 'The Bus That Honked Back' — a man makes a thing for himself; the world takes it; he stays himself
topic_candidates.reasoning: Fables are my signature (The Dragon in the Grain, Stones of the Hearth, Grundo fable pending). Tom Maneiro's story is a ready-made fable about making for yourself vs. being consumed by an audience. Cheap and fast. Risk: thematic overlap with the Grundo fable window (Aug 24); would need to space them, and the fable form can't carry the delicious factual details as well as an essay can.

topic_candidates.topic: Song: a respectful remix of the infamous title theme (Custom Song lane)
topic_candidates.reasoning: Fun, on-brand (9 songs shipped), but it's a garnish, not a meal. The joke needs context to land; music alone can't carry the story. Better as a bonus beat attached to whichever direction wins.

rejected_topics.rejection_reason: Facts without a vehicle don't move; the Grundo pattern proved the shortlist -> pick -> greenlight flow works better with directions.
Parroting the Nerd's take is the opposite of differentiated; the story's depth is the angle, not the outrage.
